analysis: Palula rhoó and Strand rhôʹ have late oo after contraction; Strand primary Phal-r.html105 explicitly cites rāva10716 and gives inflection -ʹa with ow stem material. Full Turner10716 has unaccented rāva yell, distinct from accented short ráva10641 roar. Kalkoti róo is explicitly early High and explicitly lacks Low despite Palula rh. This is a strong Palula L to Kalkoti H1 correspondence, while the absence of Low is a separate issue. The Palula h is not present in either old rava/rāva form; its chronology cannot be assumed from the modern onset alone.
unresolved: The source of the Palula breathy onset and its chronology relative to Kalkoti Low tonogenesis remain open. A regional Gawri influence is proposed by Hultman, not demonstrated by these forms alone.

analysis: Palula ordinary night róot has early oo and a-declension róota; Strand rʹôt is NTm with -a and explicitly refers to rātra10700, cross-referenced to rātri10702. The counted night/day measure raát instead has late aa and i-declension reetí. Kalkoti ordinary night ràat is therefore semantically better compared with róot when testing the Palula E to Kalkoti no-High correspondence; this removes a putative High-class mismatch but leaves Kalkoti Low unexplained by Palula h. The aa/oo comparison is also compatible with different raising histories. The dictionary rātra input has no independent accent, so no ancient barytone may be inferred just to make this fit.
unresolved: The exact common formation of Kalkoti night remains uncertain, and both rātra/rātri belong to a historically interacting night paradigm. Gawri influence may explain the extra Kalkoti Low, but is not proved. The Palula distinction should not be erased by a generic night gloss.
revision_reason: Separated ordinary night from the counted-period noun in the comparative High-tone test.
